nippert-stadium: For single-game football parking, the guide says some Woodside passes are pre-sold as accessible parking for $25. Bring that pass plus a state-issued disability placard or plate; the pass alone is insufficient. Golf carts run from outside the garage to an entry gate. Boarding, wheelchair carriage and transfer assistance are not described.

A portion of pre-sold parking in Woodside Garage will be designated as accessible parking passes for patrons with mobility issues at a rate of $25. A state-issued handicap placard or license plate will be required on Gameday with that parking pass. Anyone showing an ADA pass without a proper placard or license plate will not be permitted to park. Golf cart shuttles will run from outside the garage to the entry gate.

The football guide lists Eden Garage gameday parking at $25 by credit/debit card and describes its bus shuttles as ADA accessible. The listed campus drop-off is Commons Way at Daniels Street. Vehicle dimensions and the complete onward route have not been verified.
Gameday parking (credit/debit card only) will be available in Eden Garage for $25. Bus shuttles from Eden Garage will be ADA accessible. For more information, call (513) 556-2283.

Bus shuttles are available from Eden Garage before, during and after the game. Shuttles start 4 hours before the game starts and will continue for one hour post-game. Shuttles will drop off at the corner of Commons Way and Daniels Street. To enter Nippert Stadium, fans can walk through Sigma Sigma Commons to enter gate J, use the sidewalk to head to Fifth Third Arena and enter into Gate A or use the sidewalk to walk around the UC Baseball Stadium and down Corry Street to enter gate B.

Eden shuttle start times conflict within the football guide: one paragraph says seven hours before the game, another four hours. Both end one hour after the game. Confirm the departure time before planning an early arrival.
Shuttle buses will be running from Eden Garage to campus starting 7 hours prior to the game until 1-hour post end of the game.

Bus shuttles are available from Eden Garage before, during and after the game. Shuttles start 4 hours before the game starts and will continue for one hour post-game. Shuttles will drop off at the corner of Commons Way and Daniels Street. To enter Nippert Stadium, fans can walk through Sigma Sigma Commons to enter gate J, use the sidewalk to head to Fifth Third Arena and enter into Gate A or use the sidewalk to walk around the UC Baseball Stadium and down Corry Street to enter gate B.

The football guide recommends Gates A or B for east-side seats and G, H or J for west-side seats. Students with an ADA student-section ticket may enter any gate rather than being required to use Gate D. These gate recommendations do not establish a continuous step-free route to a seat.

Fans who are sitting on the east side of the stadium are recommended to enter through Gates A or B. Fans who are sitting on the west side of the stadium are recommended to enter through gates G, H or J. Students who acquired a ADA ticket about the student section can enter any gate and does not need to enter through gate D. Students can also reach out to the Ticket Office for additional support on entry or can get a Fast Pass wristband and enter through any gate on gameday.
UC’s accessibility page says live closed captions appear on each Nippert ribbon board, with live smartphone captions during every home game.

Fans can now view live closed captions on each ribbon board inside Nippert Stadium. In addition, live closed-captioning will be available on your smartphone during every home game. Please visit this link to view closed-captioning on your smartphone.

The football guide permits up to two unopened water bottles and prohibits other food or beverages. Its clear-bag policy allows medically necessary items after inspection; confirm arrangements for essential food or supplies before attending.
Fans are permitted to bring up to two unopened water bottles into the stadium.
Food or Beverages (excluding the two unopened water bottles)
Exceptions to this policy will be made for all medically necessary items after proper inspection.

Football FastPass wristbands are obtained by scanning tickets before gates open at the Fifth Third Arena ticket office, outside Tangeman University Center or at The Grid. The guide says guests obtaining FastPass cannot carry bags, so confirm how a medical bag affects this option.

Fans are encouraged to utilize the FastPass and to download digital tickets to make entry as smooth as possible on gameday. Fans are able to scan their tickets prior to gates opening at the Fifth Third Arena ticket office, outside TUC, or The Grid to obtain a wristband for fast entry at one of the designated gates. To obtain a FastPass, fans are not permitted to carry bags. FastPass gates are marked on the Nippert Stadium Gates Maps.

Nippert’s football guide lists lactation rooms in Tangeman University Center 432, Fifth Third Arena 432 behind section 108, and Lindner Athletic Center 338. Confirm which nearby building and room is available during the event; the guide does not describe a complete route from each stadium section.

Stadium lactation rooms:
Tangeman University Center, Room 432
Fifth Third Arena, Room 432 (Behind section 108)
Lindner Athletic Center, Room 338

For football tailgating, the guide lists lactation rooms 0012A–D and 0012 in Lindner Hall’s College of Business. From its main lobby, take the elevator to floor 00 and follow the hallway to the right. Building hours and the complete route from parking are not specified.

Lindner Hall - College of Business, Rooms 0012A, 0012B, 0012C, 0012D, 0012 Enter in the main lobby of the Lindner Hall/College of Business. If you take the steps down, take the first right and follow the hallway to the left of the elevators. If you take the elevator, go to floor 00. Once you are off the elevator, follow the hallway to the right.
fifth-third-arena: The basketball guide places restrooms mainly at the corners of both the main and upper concourses. It does not specify stall layouts, adult-changing equipment or a route from each seating area.
Restrooms are located throughout the arena, typically on the corners of both the main-level and upper-level concourses.

For men’s basketball, the guide lists shuttles between Campus Green and Dabney Circle, and University Circle and Dabney Circle, starting two hours before the game and continuing one hour afterward. It does not describe boarding equipment, wheelchair carriage or transfer assistance.
Shuttles will run between Campus Green and Dabney Circle, and between University Circle and Dabney Circle, beginning two hours before game time and one hour after the game.

For questions during basketball events, the Fan First Center is on the east concourse. Event staff, ushers or security can contact medical personnel; the First Aid center is by the Armory Bar on the north main concourse.

Have a question? Want a roster card? Need a poster? The Fan First Center is the place to go! Located on the east concourse, it's the go-to area for schedule cards, posters, roster cards and more! There are also First Game Certificates and Happy Birthday Certificates available for fans!

Emergency medical personnel are on duty at each athletics event. Medical personnel can be contacted during an event by notifying the nearest event staff member, usher, or security guard and informing them of the situation and location of the incident. The first-aid center is located on the north side of the arena on the main-level concourse by the Armory Bar.

The basketball guide lists rental lockers outside the arena’s northwest side at Lindner Athletic Building for items that cannot be brought inside. It does not give a fee, locker dimensions or a medical-equipment storage arrangement.
Lockers are available for rent outside of Fifth Third Arena on the northwest side, (Lindner Athletic Building), perfect for storing items that cannot be brought into the stadium on gameday.

For UC commencement specifically, the university directs guests needing access assistance to the far-left East Concourse doors when facing the arena, at the Oscar Robertson statue. Staff inside help with seating and accommodations. Confirm the ceremony’s arrangements; these directions are not the basketball entrance policy.
Guests with accessibility needs should enter the venue at the following location:
Fifth Third Arena - East Concourse, doors to the far left when looking at arena. East Concourse is the entrance at the Oscar Robertson basketball statue.
Once inside the venue, staff will be available to offer guidance on accessible seating and accommodations.

For UC commencement, passenger drop-off is reached by entering Woodside Drive from Martin Luther King Drive; golf carts take guests with access needs to the ceremony entrance. Guests may bring their own wheelchairs. The page does not establish cart boarding or wheelchair carriage.

For guests with accessibility needs, passenger drop-off is available by entering Woodside Drive from Martin Luther King Drive. Golf carts will shuttle guests with accessibility needs from the drop-off point to the accessibility entrance of the ceremony venue.
Guests are welcome to bring their own wheelchair to the venue if needed.
UC’s commencement guest page says ASL interpretation and live captioning are provided during the ceremony. This statement applies to commencement.
ASL interpreting and live captioning are provided during the ceremony.

For UC commencement, a free parking pass is required and accessible spaces in all parking facilities are first come, first served. Graduates receive instructions for obtaining the pass; a valid UC parking permit may also be used. This does not establish free event parking for basketball.
A free pass will be required to park on the day of the ceremony. Graduates will be emailed information on securing a free parking pass for Commencement.
Accessible parking is available in all parking facilities on a first come, first served basis.
Valid parking permit holders may utilize their UC parking permit.

UC’s single-occupancy restroom list names Shoemaker Center/Fifth Third Arena rooms 109, 323, 372, 411, 420B, 451, 486A, 4M51, 514, 588 and 686B. The list does not establish which are open to event guests, door/stall features or adult-changing equipment; ask staff for the appropriate room.
A list of single occupancy restrooms around campus is maintained by the Office of Planning, Design & Construction.
cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum: The museum’s Museums for All offer gives complimentary general admission for up to four people per SNAP EBT card with valid photo ID. It excludes ballpark tours and collectible gifts.

The Reds Hall of Fame and Museum presented by Dinsmore is excited to participate in the Museums for All program. Through this program, individuals and families presenting a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card and a valid form of photo ID are eligible for complimentary general admission to the museum. Up to four individuals can take of this offer per EBT card.
This offer is valid on general admission and does not apply to Great American Ball Park tours. Collectible gifts are not included with Museums for All admission.

The museum describes its VIP Major League Clubhouse Tour as two hours long and available only in the off-season. The stated stops include dugouts, batting tunnels and clubhouses; the page does not describe step-free alternatives, rest stops or how to arrange a modified route. Confirm those needs before booking.

The two-hour VIP Major League Clubhouse Tours are an expanded version of our standard ballpark tour that is ONLY available in the off season.
